title: Add 14-day grace period for expired licenses
description:
HIGH: When license expires, it immediately locks all features. GitLab gives 14 days grace, Grafana gives 7 days. We should follow industry standard.

**Current behavior:** License expired -> instant lockout -> all features locked -> user forced to free tier

**Desired behavior (GitLab model):**
- -30 days: Warning in LicenseBanner (yellow)
- -7 days: Urgent warning (red)  
- Day 0: License expires, enter grace period
- +7 days: Enterprise features become read-only (existing data visible, new creation blocked)
- +14 days: Full downgrade to free tier features

**Fix needed:**
1. Update src/lib/license.ts verifyLicenseOffline():
   - Add GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS = 14 constant
   - When expired but within grace period: return valid=true but add gracePeriod=true flag
   - Add daysInGracePeriod to LicenseStatus interface
2. Update src/components/LicenseBanner.tsx to show grace period warnings
3. Update src/hooks/useLicenseStatus.ts with isInGracePeriod flag
4. NEVER delete customer data on expiry - only restrict new creation

**Reference:** GitLab: 14-day grace then read-only. Grafana: 7-day grace with progressive degradation.
close_reason: Added 14-day grace period for expired licenses. During grace period: features remain functional, orange warning banner shown, error message shows days remaining. After grace period: falls back to free tier.

title: Reduce cache TTL and add clock tamper detection
description:
HIGH: Cache TTL is 1 hour - revoked licenses continue working for up to 60 minutes. No clock tamper detection means users can roll back system clock to extend expired licenses.

**Current state:**
- src/lib/license.ts: CACHE_TTL = 3600 (1 hour)
- No lastSeenTimestamp tracking
- No monotonic time check

**Fix needed:**
1. Reduce CACHE_TTL from 3600 to 300 (5 minutes) - better balance of performance vs security
2. Add clock tamper detection:
   - Store last_verified_at timestamp in app_settings when license is verified
   - On next verification, check if current time < last_verified_at (clock rolled back)
   - If clock rolled back, invalidate cache and re-verify, log warning
3. Store monotonic day counter (days_used) that only increments
4. On expiry check: compare both calendar date AND days_used against license duration

**Reference:** GitLab uses monotonic counters. CodeProject article on clock tamper detection.
close_reason: Reduced cache TTL from 3600s to 300s (5min). Added Redis-based clock tamper detection with 5min backward drift tolerance.

title: Add audit logging for license events
description:
MEDIUM: No audit trail for license changes. Cannot track who activated/removed license or when.

**Events to log:**
- license.activated: who, when, tier, features, key_hash (never full key)
- license.removed: who, when, previous_tier
- license.verified: method (offline/online), result (success/failed/expired)
- license.verification_failed: reason, source_ip
- license.feature_denied: feature_requested, current_tier, source_ip
- license.expired: when, grace_period_end
- license.grace_entered: when

**Fix needed:**
1. Create logLicenseEvent() helper in src/lib/license.ts using existing logger
2. Call it from: saveLicenseKey(), removeLicenseKey(), verifyLicense(), requireFeature()
3. Store in structured format: { event, actor, timestamp, metadata }
4. Consider adding LicenseAudit model to Prisma schema for persistent storage

**Reference:** GitLab, Grafana, n8n all log license events. OWASP recommends audit logging for all security-sensitive operations.
close_reason: Added structured audit logging for license events: activated, removed, verification_failed, grace_period_entered, grace_period_ended, clock_tamper_detected. Uses LicenseAudit logger for SIEM/ELK integration.

title: Encrypt license key at rest in database
description:
CRITICAL: License key (JWT token) is stored as plaintext in app_settings table. Anyone with DB access (backup files, SQL injection, replica) can extract and reuse the license.

**Current state in src/lib/license.ts:**
saveLicenseKey() -> prisma.appSetting.upsert({ value: licenseKey }) // PLAINTEXT!

**Fix needed:**
1. Use AES-256-GCM encryption with SESSION_SECRET (or dedicated LICENSE_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var) as key
2. Create encrypt/decrypt helpers in src/lib/license.ts
3. Encrypt before saving to DB, decrypt when reading
4. Store as 'enc:iv:ciphertext:tag' format so we know it's encrypted
5. Handle migration: if value doesn't start with 'enc:', treat as legacy plaintext and re-encrypt on next read

**Best practice:** Grafana and GitLab both encrypt sensitive data at rest.
close_reason: Added AES-256-GCM encryption for license keys stored in DB. encrypt/decrypt via scryptSync-derived key from LICENSE_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var. Backward compatible with plaintext (enc: prefix detection). Updated .env.example.

title: Add rate limiting to license API endpoints
description:
CRITICAL: No rate limiting on license APIs. Brute force and abuse possible.

**Affected endpoints (Dashboard):**
- POST /api/license - license activation (no limit)
- DELETE /api/license - license removal (no limit)
- GET /api/license - license status (no limit)

**Affected endpoints (Web app):**
- POST /api/license/generate - unlimited key generation
- POST /api/license/activate - unlimited activations
- POST /api/license/validate - unlimited validation calls
- POST /api/license/revoke - unlimited revocations

**Fix needed:**
1. Dashboard: Add rate limiting using existing rateLimit() helper from src/lib/rate-limit.ts
   - POST /api/license: 5 requests per 15 minutes
   - DELETE /api/license: 3 requests per 15 minutes
   - GET /api/license: 30 requests per minute
2. Web app: Add rate limiting middleware to all license routes
   - Generate: 10 per hour per user
   - Activate: 60 per hour per IP
   - Validate: 120 per hour per IP

**Reference:** Standard OWASP recommendation for sensitive endpoints.
close_reason: Added Redis-based rate limiting to all license API handlers: GET 30/min, POST 5/5min, DELETE 5/5min. IP-based identification with fail-closed behavior.

title: Fix activation race condition in web app
description:
CRITICAL: Race condition in license activation counter allows bypassing max_activations limit.

**Current flow in gitlab-ci-dashboard-web/src/app/api/license/activate/route.ts:**
1. Read current_activations from DB
2. Check if current_activations >= max_activations
3. UPSERT activation record
4. PostgreSQL trigger updates current_activations

**Problem:** Between steps 2 and 3, another concurrent request can also pass the check. Result: both succeed, final count exceeds limit.

**Fix needed:**
1. Use PostgreSQL SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to lock the license_keys row during check
2. Or add a CHECK constraint: current_activations <= max_activations
3. Or use atomic UPDATE ... WHERE current_activations < max_activations with row count check
4. Wrap check + upsert in a transaction with SERIALIZABLE isolation level

**Reference:** Standard database concurrency pattern. PostgreSQL advisory locks or serializable transactions.

title: Server-side feature gating for all protected API routes
description:
CRITICAL: All API endpoints (DORA metrics, dashboards, alerting, trends, history/analytics) have ZERO license checks. Feature gating is purely client-side in Sidebar.tsx and can be bypassed from browser DevTools or direct API calls.

**Current state:**
- /api/dora/metrics - NO license check (requires dora_metrics feature)
- /api/dashboards - NO license check (requires custom_dashboard feature)  
- /api/channels - NO license check (requires alerts feature)
- /api/trends - NO license check
- /api/history/analytics - NO license check

**Attack vector:** Free tier user opens browser console, calls fetch('/api/dora/metrics?projectId=1') directly - gets full DORA data without license.

**Fix needed:**
1. Create requireFeature() middleware helper in src/lib/license.ts
2. Add license checks to every protected API route
3. Map features to routes: dora_metrics -> /api/dora/*, alerts -> /api/channels/*, container_registry -> registry APIs, custom_dashboard -> /api/dashboards/*
4. Return 403 with clear error message when feature not licensed

**Reference:** GitLab, Grafana, n8n all enforce server-side feature gating.
close_reason: Server-side requireFeature() checks added to all 10 protected API route files (20+ handlers): dora/metrics, dora/deployments, dora/incidents, dashboards, channels, trends, history, history/analytics, history/export, artifacts/download
